findings.defect: The route advertises the four complementarity laws (alpha switchable at (0,0) iff not at (1,0), etc.) as content of the level theorem and their satisfaction by the blow-up table as 'a nontrivial consistency check that the shape is exactly right'. They are automatic: lem:trichotomy says that for sigma and sigma+e_i exactly one of i in S(sigma), i in S(sigma'), i in D-both holds, and a nondegenerate game has D empty -- so the improvement outmap is an orientation of the cube and the two ends of every edge disagree, for EVERY game. The check has zero discriminating power.

findings.defect: Correct and NOT vacuous (I checked the one way it could have been: all four translates B^2(.xor z), z = 8,10,24,26, are acyclic unique sink orientations, so prop:allsw-auso does not already exclude them, and the tournament is strictly stronger than acyclicity of the outer 2-face -- acyclicity forbids (P,Q,R,S) in {(1,0,1,0),(0,1,0,1)} while the tournament forbids (P,Q,R) in {(1,0,1),(0,1,0)}, and the actual violation at z=24,26 is the pattern (1,0,1,1) that acyclicity permits). But the route proves it the long way. Three lines suffice and give a much wider theorem: at layers (0,1) and (1,1) the drive solves the same equation t = R_beta.y_sigma(t)+q'_B, so w(0,1)=w(1,1); by lem:switch an improving switch raises the value vector componentwise, so along each edge of the outer 2-face y_beta is nondecreasing, whence P,Q,R ARE the three pairwise comparisons of w00,w10,w01; the patterns (1,0,1) and (0,1,0) force w00=w10=w01, and then equality of the two layer values of y_alpha through A'>0 makes alpha's margin zero, contradicting nondegeneracy. Nothing about alpha's rows (A, C_alpha, R_alpha, q_A, q'_A) is used -- so the exclusion holds for ANY nondegenerate stopping game whose outer pair satisfies only: no block row reads alpha, beta's action-1 row reads only the block, beta's action-0 row reads alpha with positive weight. dl:escape-level is not load-bearing for the route's one qualifying result.

verdict:
VERDICT: new-theorem, on ONE result, and not the one the headline leads with. Everything reproduces; nothing is false; the novelty is about a third of what is submitted.

1. THE OBJECT. The route says its object is the drive line read as a walk in the combed-flip graph. Half of that the paper already owns under its own name: def:pinned defines the driven block and the map t |-> s_B(t) verbatim, and lem:readout(a) is its analysis (retype the drive vertex as a terminal of payoff t and every readout is a minimum of at most 2^k substochastic affine maps). The round-17 novelty audit had already ruled the identical statement, rs:drive, a restatement of lem:readout(a); this route repeats it under a new name with rem:b2-anatomy as its closest label, while honestly flagging the rs:drive overlap. What IS new is the combed-flip graph -- and it does no work. dl:flippable is a correct, elementary, self-contained characterisation (I proved it by hand and checked it exhaustively over all 744 USOs of the 3-cube and all 8976 single-edge flips at m <= 3, 0 violations, plus the acyclicity law over 4256 combed flips), but the drive-line application needs only its converse half, which is three lines from lem:flat-class(a); the distance bound it supports is shown non-binding by the route's own fence count; and dl:b2-distance's table of distances is declared consequence-free by the route itself. The one result that qualifies for new-theorem, dl:no-beta-translate, does not touch the combed-flip graph at any point. The advertised object is decorative; the substance comes from extending the paper's own pinned-level machinery by two readout terms.

2. WHAT SURVIVES. dl:tournament + dl:no-beta-translate: a genuine new-relation of status refuted. rem:pinned-escape names the escape in which the layer-(0,0) outer values stop being constant and states that lem:pinned-upclosed "then says nothing"; this closes half of that escape, by a mechanism (transitivity of an order on three drives) the pinned proof never forms. I checked the one way it could have been vacuous: all four translates B^2(.xor z), z = 8,10,24,26, are acyclic unique sink orientations, so prop:allsw-auso does not already exclude them, and the tournament is strictly stronger than acyclicity of the outer 2-face -- the violation at z = 24,26 is the pattern (P,Q,R,S) = (1,0,1,1), which an acyclic square permits. The exclusion reproduces from the outmaps alone: 5 violating inner strategies at z = 24 and at z = 26, 0 at z = 8, 10 and at B^2 itself. Also surviving, at lower weight: dl:escape-level (a correct strengthening of prop:pinned-level; I re-derived all eight switchability identities and the contraction bound |Dhat|_1 + ehat < 1 by hand) and the conditional trichotomy dl:escape-mixed / dl:escape-updown with the block-specific exclusions dl:m3-decision(b),(c), whose arithmetic I reproduced exactly: the nine strategy-layer failures for z = 10 at sigma in {0,2,3,5,7} and {1,4,5,6}, and the eight psi-even <= psi-odd comparable pairs, (6,3) among them, that break up-closedness for z = 8.

3. NOT CIRCULAR, NOT VACUOUS, BUT NARROW. No target-equivalent oracle, no class, no family. This is a construction-avenue closure of exactly the genre the paper itself disclaims for cor:pinned-no-doubling: "it closes a construction avenue and is not a barrier in the sense of sec:gap; it covers none of the mechanisms M1-M6 or def:bsi." And it closes the wrong two of four: the canonical third level is B_phi(B^2, alpha_2), z = 8 (rem:blowup-measured, cor:pinned-no-doubling's "in particular the alpha_2 of B^3"), and z = 8 is precisely the translate dl:no-beta-translate does NOT cover. What the route leaves standing for z = 8 is an unproved sixteen-parameter feasibility question over one block, backed by a float search the route correctly refuses to count.

4. THE REAL REMAINING GAP, more precisely than the route states it. rem:pinned-escape asks whether a DRIVEN five-Max block that is not pinned can present B^2 at one drive and B^2(.xor z) at another. The route answers a different question -- whether a five-Max ESCAPE EXTENSION of the fixed, drive-independent three-Max block {c1,c2,c3,c6} of prop:b2-realised can have outmap B^2(.xor z) -- and answers it only for the two z carrying beta_2 (generally) and for z = 10 and the unmixed-sign z = 8 (over that one block). So after this route the open item is unchanged in kind and smaller by two corners: a driven three-Max block, possibly reading the level-three drive and possibly not the published one, carrying an escape extension with R_alpha - C_alpha mixed in sign, presenting B^2(.xor 8).

5. INTEGRATE, HEAVILY CUT -- and the paper is better for the cut half, worse for the whole.
INTEGRATE (about two pages, after cor:pinned-no-doubling, closing rem:pinned-escape's first corner): dl:escape-level, stated as what it is, the Dhat != 0 extension of prop:pinned-level, with the complementarity clause deleted (it is lem:trichotomy) and with a warning that both published realisations are pinned, so the theorem's new regime is proved and not measured; dl:tournament and dl:no-beta-translate, but GENERALISED and reproved by the short argument the route missed -- the drive is shared by the layers (0,1) and (1,1), lem:switch makes y_beta nondecreasing along every edge of the outer 2-face, so P,Q,R are the three pairwise comparisons of w00,w10,w01 and transitivity does the rest; nothing about alpha's rows is needed, so the statement holds for any nondegenerate stopping game whose outer pair satisfies only "no block row reads alpha; beta's action-1 row reads only the block; beta's action-0 row reads alpha positively", a strictly larger class than the escape shape; and dl:escape-mixed, dl:escape-updown, dl:m3-decision(b),(c) with the drive-independence of the inner block stated as a hypothesis, as cor:pinned-no-doubling states its analogue.
DO NOT INTEGRATE: dl:flippable, dl:drive-flip, dl:b2-distance and dl:sign -- a definition, a bound the route shows is never binding, a table of four distances declared consequence-free and one entry undecided, and an invariant declared to give no obstruction; a section no later result would cite, in a document whose value is that every negative claim carries a live instance. dl:fences(a),(b) -- lem:readout(a). dl:b2-line as a numbered result -- its thirteen exact fences and the fact that every one is simple belong as three lines of data inside rem:pinned-escape, credited to the round-17 correctness audit that first computed the fourteen cells.
